lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Alberto, it's Marcus from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Marcus. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hanging in there.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it 2 days, then the weekend happened.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, finding the time makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My sugar is lower in the morning when I walk after dinner.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've noticed it makes a difference.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I really want to feel like myself again. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to walk after every dinner. That's the meal that matters most for your sugar.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walks after dinner fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walks after dinner going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 4 days?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 2 out of 4 days, the hard part was finding the time, and next week you're going to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 4 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Alberto, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Reframes setback as learning in progress
Motivation: wants it for mental health too
Directive after change talk; pushes without permission
Past attempts failed; doubt about lasting
Names ambivalence: barrier versus desire to succeed
Wants to feel like himself; likes walking
Fatigue and low capacity as barrier
Insists on every dinner without permission
Sets midweek text and next call
Requests later time due to appointment

flags.reason: Directive 'You have to make this a priority' right after participant change talk on line 9; no permission asked.
'You have to walk after every dinner' pushes an absolute after sustain talk on line 21; repeated directive pattern.
Participant's 'I need this for my head too' was not explored; coach moved to persuasion.
'I really want to feel like myself again' and 'I didn't think I'd like it, but I do' went unexplored; coach switched to daughter question.

score.summary: Coach reviewed the prior week, set a concrete goal, and summarized it well, with good use of open questions about the fridge reminder and phone alarm. However, coach repeatedly used directive 'have to' statements (lines 10 and 22) and passed over several change-talk moments (lines 9 and 17), which undercut the participant's autonomy.
strengths: Line 8 and 12: reflected ambivalence and the difficulty of finding time without judgment.
Line 28 and 39: affirmed participant's ownership of the plan ('It's your plan').
Line 42: clear summary and collaborative goal confirmation with a confidence rating at line 40.
coaching_tips: Line 10 and 22: replace 'You have to' with a reflection or question, e.g., 'What would make the dinner walk feel doable?'
Line 9 and 17: when the participant voices wanting to feel like himself, ask 'Tell me more about what that would look like.'
Line 33: ask permission before offering info; it was done well at line 31, keep that pattern.
Line 18 and 20: closed questions about the daughter stalled the conversation; try an open question about support instead.
